comparison.objective: Candidate commissions a shock absorber through iterative damping adjustment; record restocks a twin-roll dispenser in the required stub/new-roll order and locks its cover.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, setscrew loosening/retightening, fine collar rotation, and response-driven tuning. Record requires tab-held core removal/insertion, sprung-hub engagement, gate movement, and cover release/latching.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate needs two safe physical impact cycles within stroke, rebound, overload, hard-stop, and drift limits. Record needs correctly engaged rolls on designated hubs, gate clear, cover latched, objects released and still, with drop/slam/misseating failures.
comparison.reason: Both include bimanual stabilization and locking, but the tested abilities differ materially: dynamic damper commissioning with tool torque and iterative response control versus sequenced roll exchange through sprung hubs. Candidate omits numeric drift tolerance, rebound/overload definitions, and setscrew torque; those gaps do not create plausible duplication.
